questions.note: Order now reads right: hallux about 5 mm ahead of toe 2 in plan, 3 to 5 descending. Shaping gives it away: from above the toes are slender fingers with bead knuckles and dark clefts to the webs; from below matchstick stalks with ring bands; from the side crumpled tips. The 5th toe sits lower but stands nail up beside the 4th, not curled under it.

Anterior crease now present and the front of the ankle bends tighter. But the lateral malleolus is a long soft swelling with no tip, the medial one barely swells the outline in V8, the heel meets the lateral malleolus at a ledge, the ankle above the malleoli is a parallel column, and the side silhouette has no Achilles waist.

defects.what: From above all five toes stand apart like fingers: dark clefts run from the tips almost to the webs, the hallux-toe 2 slot reaches back to the ball, and toes 2-4 are slim shafts with bead knuckles.
defects.fix: Real toes press side by side, broadest at the web, the clefts short and closed by soft tissue; knuckles are low swells on plump toes.

defects.what: The heel from behind is still a box with rounded corners: parallel vertical sides, a flat bottom and a squared shoulder at the top where it meets the ankle.
defects.fix: From behind the heel is a bell: widest at the pad, its sides converging upward into the Achilles without a shoulder.

defects.what: The lateral ankle reads as two stacked lumps, the malleolus above and the heel flank below, with a notch between them; the same ledge shows in V8 at about [580, 973, 683, 1118].
defects.fix: One continuous form runs from the fibular tip down through the peroneal hollow into the heel's side.

defects.what: The lateral malleolus is a long soft swelling on the outline with no apex; in V3 it is a broad mound beside a blurred dark hollow.
defects.fix: A narrower bony knob whose pointed tip stands clear above and in front of the hollow below it.

defects.what: The medial malleolus barely swells the medial outline in V8 and is invisible in V1f, so the ankle reads one-sided.
defects.fix: A broad round bony dome, higher than the lateral, about 5 mm proud of the shin line.

defects.what: The back of the ankle in the side silhouette runs straight down and then slants out into the heel: no concave Achilles waist above the calcaneus.
defects.fix: The Achilles cord stands behind a concave dip just above the heel's bulge.

defects.what: From behind the ankle above the malleoli is a parallel-sided column almost as wide as the heel; the Achilles is a soft ridge on it rather than a cord standing out from hollows.
defects.fix: A lean man's ankle narrows above the malleoli to the Achilles with deep retro-malleolar hollows either side.

defects.what: The sole is a blank smooth slab with a shallow central trough: only a faint heel-pad edge and ball band, no lateral weight band, no arch hollow, no plump ball pad.
defects.fix: A heel pad, a lateral band to the 5th head, a deep medial arch hollow and a rounded ball pad behind a toe sulcus.

defects.what: From below the lesser toes are matchstick stalks with ring bands and ball tips, pinched where they join the sole.
defects.fix: Plantar toes are a row of plump pads with soft creases, set behind a deep sulcus.

defects.what: A Y-shaped pinch crease on the lateral sole, a mesh artefact.
defects.fix: Relax the surface there; the sole has no fold at that spot.

defects.what: The 1st MTP is a round knob with a neck in front of it, reading as a bunion; the plan view shows the same knob jutting from the medial border.
defects.fix: The medial eminence is a broad, low, smooth swell that flows into the hallux without a waist.

defects.what: From the side the toe tips are crimped and crumpled, with a notched 5th-toe nub, like crumpled plastic tubes.
defects.fix: Each toe ends in a smooth pulp bulge under the nail, with a clean curve over the tip.

defects.what: Seven or eight thin, evenly spaced, sharp-edged tendon cords run down the dorsum into the toes, the crispest relief on the foot, so it reads cabled rather than domed.
defects.fix: The extensors show as a few low, soft-edged ridges that fade into the dorsum's fat, clearest only toward the toes.

defects.what: A thin dashed vertical seam line still runs below the medial malleolus in V2.
defects.fix: Weld or relax the seam; the skin is continuous there.

defects.what: A small round pit on the flat medial midfoot reads as a dent; no navicular tuberosity and almost no readable arch vault.
defects.fix: One long smooth vault with a small navicular dome above the full abductor hallucis.

defects.what: The 5th metatarsal styloid is a round marble under the skin.
defects.fix: A low, elongated tuberosity blending into the lateral border.

defects.what: The 5th toe sits lower but still stands beside the 4th with its nail facing up and a cleft between them, a small copy of the 4th.
defects.fix: Rotated onto its side, curled, and tucked against or under the 4th, the nail facing outward.

defects.what: The tibialis anterior is missing: the front of the ankle is smooth apart from the crease lines.
defects.fix: A broad cord medial of the crease running from the shin to the medial midfoot, the strongest landmark at a lean man's ankle front.

defects.what: The lateral side of the foot is one flat, featureless wall from heel to 5th head, like a shoe last.
defects.fix: A soft extensor digitorum brevis swell in front of the lateral malleolus, the styloid bump, and the lateral border rounding down to the floor.

defects.what: The hallux IP crease is still a single ring band around the toe.
defects.fix: A few soft, short, uneven wrinkles over the joint that fade at the sides.

defects.what: A sharp vertical slit or fold at the root of the hallux-toe 2 web.
defects.fix: A smooth web commissure.

defects.what: A small dark tick mark on the skin just above the 5th toe's nail.
defects.fix: Clean surface; check for a stray edge or inverted face.

defects.what: A thin spike sticks out of the silhouette at the 4-5 toe cleft.
defects.fix: No spike: the cleft's edge is smooth.

ranked: [D1] From above the toes are a hand's fingers: separate shafts with bead knuckles and dark clefts nearly to the webs. A man's toes press together, broadest at the web, short and fleshy.
[D2] The heel from behind is still a rounded box with parallel sides and a flat bottom; a real heel is a bell narrowing up into the Achilles.
[D8] The sole is a mannequin slab with a central trough: no lateral band, arch hollow or ball pad.
[D9] Plantar toes are matchstick stalks with ring bands and ball tips instead of plump pads behind a sulcus.
[D3] The lateral ankle reads as two stacked lumps with a notch between, the heel stuck on below the malleolus.
[D4] The lateral malleolus is a long soft swelling with no pointed tip; [D5] the medial one barely shows, so the ankle reads one-sided.
[D7] The ankle above the malleoli is a column nearly as wide as the heel, with the Achilles only a soft ridge; a lean man's ankle narrows hard there.
[D6] No Achilles waist in the side silhouette: the back line runs straight into the heel bulge.
[D13] The dorsum carries seven or eight thin, even, crisp tendon cords: the sharpest relief on the foot, reading as cables laid on a smooth dome.
Over the whole foot the surface is one rubbery smoothness with detail crisp only in cords and crease lines; no fat-pad softness, no skin folds: it reads cast, not grown.
[D11] The 1st MTP is a round knob with a neck in front, a bunion instead of the broad low swell of the ball.
[D17] The 5th toe stands nail up beside the 4th, a small copy of it, not rotated and tucked under.
[D12] From the side the toe tips are crimped and crumpled, like wrinkled plastic tubes.
[D19] The lateral side of the foot is a flat shoe-last wall with no extensor brevis swell or rounded border.
[D16] The styloid is a round marble under the skin, not a low elongated tuberosity.
[D15] The medial midfoot is flat with a round pit; no navicular dome and a weak arch vault in V2.
[D18] No tibialis anterior cord at the front of the ankle, the strongest landmark there on a lean man.
[D14] A dashed seam line still runs below the medial malleolus in V2.
The veins are declared, but they are so thick and crisp that they notch the dorsal silhouette in V2o and the medial border in V4o, which hides the true profile of the instep.
[D10] A Y-shaped pinch crease on the lateral sole, a mesh artefact.
[D20] The hallux IP crease is a single ring band rather than a few soft wrinkles.
[D21] A sharp slit at the root of the hallux-toe 2 web in V5f.
[D22] A dark tick mark above the 5th toe's nail in V5f.
[D23] A thin spike in the plantar silhouette at the 4-5 cleft.
